feature_candidates.description: Weight user historical long_view by a per-tab half-life based on event recency (hourmin) so recent interactions matter more within each tab.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Capture differential engagement decay across tabs, improving nDCG@5 given tab4's much higher long_view.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Extend history_features to compute per-tab decayed prior using training-time hourmin differences.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; derived strictly from training history timestamps, no future data.
feature_candidates.name: Tab-stratified recency decay weights

feature_candidates.description: Add log(video_age_in_days+1) as a feature conditioned on tab to model novelty effects on long_view propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Distinguish old vs new videos differently per tab; tab4 may prefer newer content, improving ranking.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute video age from video table (non-leaky) relative to train timestamps; concatenate with tab embedding.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if age uses train-period reference epoch; must avoid validation/test future dates.
feature_candidates.name: Video age × tab interaction

feature_candidates.description: User's historical long_view rate per author within each tab, smoothed, to strengthen preference signals.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Better exploit author affinity inside a tab, especially where author–tab patterns are stable.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add (user_author, tab) aggregation to history_features pipeline.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; uses user interaction history only, must exclude current-row interaction during train.
feature_candidates.name: Author-tab cross aggregate for user history

findings.implication: Incorporating tab interaction into history_features (e.g., per-tab historical rates and decay) should improve within-user ranking.
findings.observation: Tab4 has 48.93% long_view rate vs 38.61% for tab1 and 4.22% for tab0, with 73% of rows in tab1.
findings.title: Tab-specific long_view propensity is highly differential

findings.implication: Further refinement of history_features (video age, author-tab) is more promising than loss-function tuning.
findings.observation: hist_prior_days_var_gs2_3b9a achieves primary 0.6045 (GAUC 0.6707, nDCG 0.5382), while BPR and group_softmax only reach ~0.55.
findings.title: history_features with tab×recency dominates classic losses

findings.implication: Derived per-video long_view propensity must remain diagnostic; time-safe recency and user history features should be used instead.
findings.observation: Implied exposures ~12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged (≈4892:1); observation periods exceed log span.
findings.title: Video statistics table is leaky and unusable for training

expected_artifacts: Per-tab long_view rate bucketed by recency (hourmin, days since upload) tables and plots from train split
Correlation matrix between video statistics long_view propensity and observed long_view in train, stratified by tab
Histogram and coverage report of video age, including zero-duration and sentinel rows
Summary of user history feature coverage and missingness to guide history_features preprocessing
feature_hypotheses: Adding tab-specific recency decay weights to history_features will improve long_view ranking, as tab 4 has notably higher long_view rate than tab 1.
Video age in days (or its log) interacting with tab will capture novelty effects and is compatible with the history_features family.
A user's historical long_view rate for a given author (use_user_author) can be strengthened by including author-tab cross aggregates.
The video statistics long_view propensity (if used) must be time-bucketed or otherwise treated as a noisy prior to avoid leakage-induced overfitting.
leakage_risks: Using video statistics period aggregates may leak future information; any derived feature must be only a diagnostic, not used for training unless explicitly debiased.
Temporal leakage if recency features use future timestamps from validation/test period; all time-based features must be computed strictly from training history.
Rare tabs (e.g., tabs 3,5,7-14) have very few samples and may cause unstable per-tab statistics; consider merging or excluding.
Sentinel values (is_live_streamer=-124) and zero-duration videos might distort user/video aggregates if not handled explicitly.
plan.objective: Explore train/validation data to identify differential long_view patterns across tabs, recency, and video features that can inform history_features variant selection for within-user ranking.
questions: How does long_view rate vary by hourmin and day-of-week within each tab in the training log?
What is the distribution of video age (days since upload) and how does long_view propensity change with age conditional on tab?
Does the leaky video statistics table provide a per-video long_view propensity that correlates with observed long_view beyond what history_features already captures?
How do sentinel values (is_live_streamer=-124) and zero-duration videos affect user history aggregation and should they be filtered or imputed?
required_inputs: Training interaction log (train split) with columns: user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, label long_view
Video feature table including video age, duration, upload_type, and other static attributes
User profile table including active_degree, is_live_streamer sentinel, etc.
Video statistics table (marked as leaky) for exploratory correlation analysis only

report.recommended_next_focus: Refine history_features with per-tab recency decay and video-age interaction, while keeping video statistics out of training due to leakage.
report.summary: Within-user long_view ranking is best served by history_features with tab-specific recency and author cross-aggregates; tab4 shows far higher long_view (48.93%) than tab1 (38.61%) and tab0 (4.22%). Video statistics are period aggregates over full platform traffic and are leaky; use only for diagnostics.
